tasks.short: Take payment and make change at the booth, count and balance the cash drawer, record the drawer total, and hand over the deposit and split tips.

steps.what: Customer pays the parking fee in cash at the booth
Parking attendant takes cash and makes change
Parking attendant counts and balances the cash drawer at the end of the shift
Parking attendant records the drawer total on the shift sheet
Parking attendant hands over the deposit bag
Parking attendant works out and distributes tips

tasks.design: Card terminals and pay-by-app at the exit take most payments, so less cash passes the booth. The till ({OTHER}) shows the expected cash per shift, the attendant counts and confirms the drawer, and the till writes the shift record. Card tips are split by the till. Handing over the deposit stays with the attendant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most customers paid cash and every shift was balanced on a paper sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Card terminals and parking apps are common at garage exits.
tasks.still_hard: Some customers will only pay cash.
tasks.human_edge: Settling a wrong-change claim without losing the customer.

evidence.claim: Garage tills show expected cash per shift and take card payments at the exit.

assumptions: Boundary: from the customer's payment to the deposit handed over; bank deposits are outside.
Input contract: tariffs set by the garage manager in the till; fallback is cash and the paper sheet.
Customers paying by card or app spend about the same time as paying cash; their time is priced as customer time.
Handing over the deposit does not change.
Handing over the deposit bag (s5) keeps its full time; only working out tips (s6) is priced, for the card tips the till splits.

incremental.description: Parking attendant helps customers whose card or app fails.
Customers pay by card or app at the exit themselves.

approvals.approved_version: The drawer count as confirmed by the attendant in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many customers keep paying cash; high: most pay by card or app.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Calculate the charge from the entry ticket and tariff, explain it to the customer, collect the fee, handle complaints and lost tickets, and record refunds.

steps.what: Customer asks what they owe at the exit
Parking attendant calculates parking charges from the entry ticket and tariff card
Parking attendant explains the charge to the customer
Parking attendant collects fees from customers
Parking attendant responds to customer complaints and lost tickets
Parking attendant pays refunds and writes them in the logbook

tasks.design: A camera reads the licence plate at entry, and the parking system ({OTHER}) computes the charge from the entry time and the tariff table, showing the breakdown on the exit screen. Customers pay by card at the terminal. Refunds are paid back to the card from the till after the attendant decides, and the till records them. Complaints and lost tickets stay with the attendant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charges were worked out from paper tickets and the tariff card, and refunds written in a logbook.
tasks.enabler_now: Licence plate cameras and parking systems compute charges from entry times.
tasks.still_hard: Plates that the camera misreads still need the attendant.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a customer who is late for a hospital appointment.
tasks.altitude: The attendant handles disputes instead of every calculation.

evidence.claim: Parking systems compute charges from licence plate entry times and tariff tables.
Cameras on public space need a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from the customer's question to the recorded refund; tariff setting is outside.
Input contract: tariff table set by the garage manager; plate reads from the entry camera; fallback is paper tickets.
Customers read the charge on the exit screen and pay by card themselves; about the same time, priced as customer time.
Complaints and refund decisions stay with the attendant.

incremental.description: Customers read the charge breakdown on the exit screen.

approvals.approved_version: The refund as decided by the attendant in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an older garage with paper tickets at most exits; high: plate cameras and card terminals at all exits.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Give directions and information, help customers with wheelchairs and luggage, and answer phone questions about rates and hours.

steps.what: Parking attendant gives directions and information to customers
Parking attendant helps customers with wheelchairs and luggage
Customers phone the booth about rates and opening hours
Parking attendant answers phone questions about rates and opening hours

tasks.design: A garage page on the website ({CMS}) and QR codes on the signs show rates, opening hours, walking routes and the nearest wheelchair-accessible lift, so fewer customers need to ask or phone. Giving directions in person and helping with wheelchairs and luggage stay with the attendant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every question about rates, hours and routes came to the booth.
tasks.enabler_now: Garage pages and QR signs give rates, hours and routes on a phone.
tasks.still_hard: Older and confused customers still need someone to walk with them.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a customer struggling with a wheelchair and stepping in.

reach.learn: Whether the page cuts phone calls.

evidence.claim: Garage web pages and QR codes on signs can show rates, hours and walking routes.

assumptions: Boundary: from the customer's question to the answer or help given; complaints are outside.
Input contract: rates and hours kept by the garage manager on the page; fallback is asking at the booth.
Customers look up rates on the page instead of phoning; about the same time, priced as customer time.
Helping in person does not change.

incremental.description: Parking attendant reports wrong information on the page.
Customers look up rates and routes on the garage page.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many older visitors who ask in person; high: mostly regular commuters who use the page.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Spot incidents on camera or on rounds, call emergency responders with the location, help motorists such as jump-starting a stalled car, and write the incident report.

steps.what: Parking attendant spots incidents and stalled vehicles on camera or on rounds
Parking attendant calls emergency responders or the proper authorities and gives the location
Parking attendant provides motorist assistance such as helping jump start a stalled vehicle
Parking attendant writes an incident report on paper

tasks.design: A short incident form on the booth terminal ({OTHER}) fills in time, level and the nearest camera, so the attendant adds only what happened. Spotting incidents, calling responders and helping motorists stay with the attendant; no automatic call is made.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incident reports were handwritten after the event.
tasks.enabler_now: Booth terminals can host short incident forms linked to cameras.
tasks.still_hard: Emergencies leave no time for forms until afterwards.
tasks.human_edge: Staying calm and giving responders the right entrance.

reach.learn: Whether structured reports show repeat problem spots.

evidence.claim: Booth terminals can host short incident forms that fill in time and location.
Cameras on public space need a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from garage activity to the incident report; insurance claims are outside.
Input contract: camera locations set by the garage manager; fallback is a paper form.
Spotting, calling and helping do not change.
research_questions: Do reports reach the manager the same day?

incremental.description: Parking attendant fills in fields the form cannot prefill.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few incidents a month; high: a large garage with frequent breakdowns.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The parking attendant keeps helping customers and motorists, settling disputes and calling responders; calculating charges, balancing paper sheets, routine questions and handwritten reports shrink.
skills_to_grow: Handling card and app payment problems
role.ambitious_version: An attendant who spends the day helping people rather than handling coins.
